To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy deposits of muon bundles detected by the NEVOD detector increase rapidly with increasing zenith angle.

the average energy deposited by muons in bundles detected in the NEVOD detector grows with the zenith angle and that the energy of muons in the bundles is much higher than that of the muons in the showers.
muon bundles detected by the NEVOD EAS array at zenith angles of 60°–90° contain muons with energies of ∼500 Gev, while the muon density is ∼1 muon/m ^{2}.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the energy characteristics of inclined muon showers in EAS.
the development of new methods for the study of the energy characteristics of inclined EAS muon components.
the study of the energy characteristics of inclined EAS muon bundles in the Cherenkov calorimetric detector NEVOD on the Earth’s suface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy characteristics of inclined muon showers are not well understood.
the energy deposit of the muon bundles in the Cherenkov water calorimeter depends on zenith angle and the local muon bundle density, and the muon energy in the bundles grows with zenith angle.
, in the case of inclined muon showers, the energy of the primary particles is higher than that of the vertical muons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first who have measured the muon bundle energies at the Earth’s surface and found that they are comparable to those of the muon bundles measured in underground muon detectors.
muon bundles with energies of ∼1 TeV are detected on the Earth’s sufrace.
the muon bundles are a promising source of information for the study of the EAS muon energy spectrum and its zenith angle dependence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy characteristics of the muons in the bundles are significantly different from those in individual muons.
the average energy per muon in a bundle is higher than that for a single muon.

muon energy deposits in the Cherenkov detector are sensitive to changes in the EAS muon energy spectrum in the energy range of 10–1000 GeV, and this sensitivity can be used to study the energy spectrum of muons from inclined EAS.
